ai.literal: He who is called a householder is a support standing in the good path for the three who have natural duties.
ai.translation: He who is said to live the domestic life is a steadfast support in the righteous path for the three classes of people who follow their natural duties.
ai.modern: இல்வாழ்க்கை வாழ்பவன் என்று சொல்லப்படுபவன், தன் இயல்புடைய மூன்று பிரிவினருக்கும் நல்ல வழியில் நிலைத்து நிற்கும் துணையாவான்.
ai.explanation: This couplet defines the primary role of a householder (இல்வாழ்வான்) as a pillar of support for three other groups of people (மூவர்) who depend on him. These three groups represent individuals in other stages of life who cannot sustain themselves. The householder must support them not just materially, but by remaining firmly established in the 'good path' (நல்லாறு) of virtue. By staying righteous himself, he becomes a reliable 'support' (துணை) that enables others to fulfill their own natural duties.

ai.literal: To those who have renounced, and to the destitute, and to those who have passed away, he who is called a householder is a support.
ai.translation: The householder is the support for those who have renounced the world, the destitute who cannot support themselves, and the departed who have passed away.
ai.modern: துறவிகளுக்கும், வறுமையில் உள்ளவர்களுக்கும், இறந்தவர்களுக்கும் இல்லறத்தில் வாழ்பவனே துணையாவான்.
ai.explanation: This couplet defines the social and moral duties of a householder by identifying three groups that depend on him. 'துறந்தார்' refers to ascetics who have renounced material life and rely on others for food. 'துவ்வாதவர்' refers to the poor and helpless who cannot secure their own livelihood. 'இறந்தார்' refers to ancestors or deceased relatives whose memory and rites are preserved by the living. By sustaining these three groups, the householder serves as their essential support (துணை).

ai.literal: Ancestors, gods, guests, relatives, oneself, saying thus, to cherish these five ways is the foremost duty.
ai.translation: To cherish the fivefold duties toward ancestors, gods, guests, relatives, and oneself is the householder's foremost duty.
ai.modern: தென்புலத்தார் (முன்னோர்), தெய்வம், விருந்தினர், சுற்றத்தார், தான் ஆகிய ஐந்து இடங்களிலும் செய்ய வேண்டிய கடமைகளைப் போற்றிச் செய்தல் இல்லறத்தானுக்கு முதன்மையான கடமையாகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet outlines the five essential duties of a householder. The five categories are tenpulattār (ancestors), teyvam (gods), viruntu (guests), okkal (relatives), and tāṉ (oneself). The word ōmpal means to cherish or protect, indicating that these are active duties of support. The poet concludes that fulfilling these five obligations is the talai (foremost or supreme) duty of domestic life.

ai.literal: If life possesses food shared while fearing blame, the failing of lineage at any time is not.
ai.translation: If a householder's life consists of sharing food with others while fearing blame, their lineage will never die out.
ai.modern: பழிக்கு அஞ்சி, உணவைப் பிறரோடு பகிர்ந்து உண்ணும் தன்மையைக் கொண்டதாக இல்வாழ்க்கை இருக்குமானால், அவருடைய சந்ததி எப்போதும் அழியாது.
ai.explanation: This couplet highlights the core virtues of a householder: avoiding blame and sharing food with those in need. The word 'paḻi' refers to the moral dread of acquiring wealth through unjust means, while 'pāttu' emphasizes the duty of hospitality and charity. The poet promises that a household run on these two principles will never see its lineage die out. Thus, ethical living combined with active benevolence ensures the eternal continuity and prosperity of one's family.

ai.literal: And love and virtue if possesses domestic life, and quality and fruit that.
ai.translation: If domestic life possesses love and virtue, that is both its true character and its ultimate fruit.
ai.modern: குடும்ப வாழ்க்கை அன்பையும் அறத்தையும் கொண்டதாக இருக்குமானால், அதுவே அவ்வாழ்க்கையின் பண்பும் பயனும் ஆகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet defines the essence and purpose of a householder's life. If a family life is built upon love among its members and virtue towards the world, it achieves its true state. Here, love represents the internal quality or character of the home, while virtue represents the external fruit or benefit it yields to society. Thus, love and virtue are not just ornaments but the very definition and reward of domestic life.

ai.literal: Of virtue in the path domestic life if one conducts, on the outside path having gone, what is to be gained?
ai.translation: If one conducts domestic life in the path of virtue, what is there to be gained by leaving it and entering other paths?
ai.modern: அறநெறியில் இல்லற வாழ்க்கையை நடத்தினால், அதை விட்டுவிட்டு வேறு நெறிகளில் சென்று பெறுவது என்ன இருக்கிறது?
ai.explanation: This couplet emphasizes that a righteous domestic life is the highest path of virtue. If a householder conducts their family life according to moral principles, there is no need to wander away in search of other spiritual or ascetic paths. The word 'போஒய்' is a poetic elongation of 'போய்' (having gone), highlighting the unnecessary effort of seeking external paths. The rhetorical question 'பெறுவது எவன்' (what is to be gained?) shows that true fulfillment is already fully realized within a virtuous home.

ai.literal: He who lives the domestic life by its natural duty is called the foremost among all those who strive.
ai.translation: He who lives the domestic life in accordance with its natural virtue is the foremost among all those who strive for spiritual liberation.
ai.modern: அறநெறியின் இயல்போடு இல்லற வாழ்க்கை வாழ்பவன், நற்கதிக்காக முயலும் மற்ற எல்லோரையும் விட முதன்மையானவன் ஆவான்.
ai.explanation: This couplet highlights the supreme value of a righteous householder. The word 'இயல்பு' refers to the natural, virtuous duties of a householder, which include supporting others and living selflessly. The poet compares this householder to 'முயல்வார்', those who perform intense spiritual penance or strive for liberation. By declaring the householder as 'தலை' (the foremost), the couplet teaches that fulfilling one's domestic duties virtuously is superior to escaping the world through asceticism.

ai.literal: Guiding others in the right path, without deviating from virtue, a domestic life possesses greater power of endurance than those who perform penance.
ai.translation: A domestic life that guides others in the right path and does not itself deviate from virtue possesses greater power of endurance than the penance of ascetics.
ai.modern: பிறரை நல்வழியில் செலுத்தி, தானும் அறநெறியிலிருந்து தவறாமல் வாழ்கின்ற இல்லற வாழ்க்கை, தவம் செய்வோரின் தவ வலிமையை விடவும் சிறந்த வலிமையைக் கொண்டதாகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet compares the moral strength of a householder with that of an ascetic. The poet states that a domestic life (இல்வாழ்க்கை) has greater power of endurance (நோன்மை) than the penance of ascetics (நோற்பார்). This is because the householder must guide others along the path of virtue (ஆற்றின் ஒழுக்கி) while ensuring they do not slip from righteousness themselves (அறனிழுக்கா). While ascetics only endure personal hardships, a householder must support others to live virtuously while maintaining their own integrity, which requires far greater moral fortitude.

ai.literal: Virtue as called indeed is household life; and that too, if others' blame is not there, is good.
ai.translation: What is called virtue is indeed the household life; and even that is excellent only if it is free from the blame of others.
ai.modern: அறம் என்று சொல்லப்பட்டது இல்வாழ்க்கையே ஆகும்; அதுவும் பிறர் பழிக்கும் குற்றம் இல்லாமல் இருந்தால் மிகவும் நல்லது.
ai.explanation: This couplet defines the true nature of virtue by identifying it directly with the life of a householder. The poet asserts that domestic life itself is the primary form of virtue. However, a crucial condition is added: this household life is truly good and noble only if it is lived without giving others any cause for blame. Thus, a blameless domestic life is presented as the highest moral path.

ai.literal: He who lives on earth in the way one ought to live, among the gods dwelling in heaven will be placed.
ai.translation: He who lives his domestic life on earth as it should be lived will be counted among the gods who dwell in heaven.
ai.modern: உலகத்தில் வாழ வேண்டிய நெறிமுறைப்படி வாழ்பவன், வானுலகத்தில் வாழும் தேவர்களுள் ஒருவனாக வைத்து மதிக்கப்படுவான்.
ai.explanation: This couplet highlights the greatness of a householder who leads a righteous life. The author states that one who fulfills the duties of domestic life properly on earth does not need to seek divinity elsewhere; they are already equal to the gods dwelling in heaven. The key words 'வாழ்வாங்கு வாழ்பவன்' (he who lives as one ought to live) emphasize that the manner of living is more important than mere existence. Such a person is elevated to divine status, as indicated by 'தெய்வத்துள் வைக்கப்படும்' (will be placed among the gods).
